content.text: Hajjar car dealership - Prototype
Overview

The Hajjar Car Dealership system is designed to manage the inventory, sales, and customer interactions of a multi-location automotive dealership. It provides a centralized platform for tracking vehicles from acquisition to sale, managing sales staff performance, and maintaining customer relationships.
Note: This specification represents a prototype version of the system that will be further enhanced and expanded in future iterations.
Requirements
1. Inventory Management
The system shall track vehicles across multiple locations, including the primary Beirut location.
Each vehicle record must include: VIN (Unique Identifier), LocationID, Make, Model, Year, Trim, Color, Mileage, Engine Type, Transmission, and Status (Available, Reserved, Sold, In-Service).
The system shall validate the VIN against standard 17-character formats (ISO 3779).
The system shall support both New and Pre-owned vehicle categories.
For Pre-owned vehicles, the system shall allow attaching condition reports and photos.
Administrators shall be able to update vehicle pricing and promotional discounts.
Vehicle status transitions must follow a safety-first workflow: vehicles in 'In-Service' status must return to 'Available' (triggering a safety inspection log) before they can be marked as 'Sold'.
2. Sales Management
The system shall record sales transactions, including the vehicle sold, the customer, the sales representative, the final sale price, and the date of sale.
The system shall ensure the 'final sale price' cannot be lower than the vehicle's cost without explicit Sales Manager approval.
It shall support different payment methods: Cash, Finance, and Lease.
For Finance and Lease transactions, the system shall record external financing entity details and lienholder information.
The system shall track the status of external financing applications using a state machine (e.g., Pending, Approved, Rejected).
The system shall track trade-in vehicles associated with a sale, including their appraisal value.

When a trade-in is recorded, the vehicle is automatically added to the inventory as 'Pre-owned'. The system shall prompt for a new LocationID and set the initial Status to 'In-Service' for inspection.
3. Customer Management
The system shall maintain a database of customers with contact information (Name, Email, Phone, Address).
It shall track customer interaction history, including test drives and previous purchases.
4. Staff and Roles
The system shall support role-based access control for different user types: Admin, Sales Manager, Sales Representative, and Service Technician.
Sales Representatives shall be assigned to specific locations but may view inventory across all locations.
Open Questions
Should the system integrate with external vehicle history providers (e.g., CARFAX)?
Is a service/maintenance module required for tracking repairs on inventory or customer vehicles?
How should the system handle online reservations and deposits?

comments.text: This requirement contradicts the 'Overview' which describes a 'multi-location' system. If the system is meant to be multi-location, the data schema must support a 'LocationID' for every vehicle rather than hardcoding for Beirut.
For Finance and Lease transactions, the system shall record external financing entity details and lienholder information.
The specification lacks a requirement for tracking the status of these external applications (e.g., Pending, Approved, Rejected). Suggest adding a state machine for financing workflows.
yes 100%
Sales Representatives shall be assigned to specific locations but may view inventory across all locations.

The document should clarify if Sales Representatives have 'Read-Only' access to other locations or if they can initiate a 'Reserved' status for a vehicle located at a different branch to prevent double-selling.
defer
The system shall maintain a database of customers with contact information (Name, Email, Phone, Address).
To comply with data privacy regulations (like GDPR or local equivalents), the system should include a requirement for capturing and logging customer consent for marketing and data retention.
Defer this and reply here that you defered it without resolving the comment
I have deferred this requirement as requested. It is currently not included in the spec.
The system shall track trade-in vehicles associated with a sale, including their appraisal value.

When a trade-in is recorded, the system should specify if that vehicle is automatically added to the inventory as 'Pre-owned'. If so, the spec needs to define the workflow for assigning a new LocationID and Status to the trade-in vehicle.
The system shall support both New and Pre-owned vehicle categories.

There is no mention of how 'Condition' or 'Damage Reports' are handled for Pre-owned vehicles. Suggest adding a requirement for attaching condition reports or photos to differentiate between new and used inventory quality.
The system shall record sales transactions, including the vehicle sold, the customer, the sales representative, the final sale price, and the date of sale.

The specification lacks a validation rule to ensure the 'final sale price' cannot be lower than a minimum threshold (or 'cost') without Sales Manager approval. This is critical for preventing unauthorized discounts at the Sales Representative level.
VIN (Unique Identifier)

The specification identifies VIN as the unique identifier but does not define a validation strategy. Suggest adding a requirement to validate the VIN against standard 17-character formats (ISO 3779) to prevent data entry errors in the inventory system.
Status (Available, Reserved, Sold, In-Service)

There is no defined logic for status transitions. For example, the system should specify if a vehicle can move directly from 'In-Service' to 'Sold' or if it must first return to 'Available' to ensure safety inspections are logged.
